lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Income taxes payable, non-current
lines.why: Taxes on operating income due after a year (often uncertain tax positions): operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

No other customer or distributor represented more than 10 percent of net sales in fiscal years 2026, 2025, or 2024.

International sales represented 99 percent of our net sales in fiscal years 2026, 2025, and 2024.
HPMS product line sales of $837.4 million represented a 10 percent increase from fiscal year 2025 sales of $758.9 million, largely attributable to demand for components shipping into smartphones.

International sales, including sales to U.S.-based end customers that manufacture products through contract manufacturers or plants located overseas, were approximately $2.0 billion, $1.9 billion, and $1.8 billion in fiscal years 2026, 2025, and 2024, respectively, representing 99 percent of net sales in fiscal years 2026, 2025, and 2024.
For fiscal years 2026, 2025 and 2024, our ten largest end customers represented approximately 96 percent, 96 percent and 95 percent of our net sales, respectively.
We use a variety of foundries in the production of wafers, primarily supplied by GLOBALFOUNDRIES Inc., ("GlobalFoundries") and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, Limited ("TSMC").
We rely on patent, copyright, trademark, and trade secret laws to protect our intellectual property, products, and technology.

Our future success may also depend on assisting our customers with integration of our components into their new products, including providing support from the concept stage through design, launch and production ramp.

We depend on a limited number of customers and distributors for a substantial portion of our sales, and the loss of, or a significant reduction in orders from, or pricing on products sold to, any key customer or distributor could significantly reduce our sales and our profitability.

Because we depend on subcontractors internationally to perform key manufacturing functions for us, we are subject to political, economic, climate and natural disaster risks that could disrupt the fabrication, assembly, packaging, or testing of our products.
We depend on third-party subcontractors, primarily in Asia, for the fabrication, assembly, packaging, and testing of most of our products.

Although we seek to reduce our dependence on any one subcontractor, the substantial majority of our semiconductor wafers are manufactured by TSMC at fabs in Taiwan, and GlobalFoundries in Singapore and Germany.
Transferring from a primary supplier to another facility would likely result in increased production costs and a delay in production.
In general, we rely on customers issuing purchase orders to buy our products rather than long-term supply contracts.

We depend on the use of information technology systems; disruptions to these systems could impact our ability to perform necessary business operations and have an adverse impact on our financial condition.
While we own and manage some of these information technology systems directly, we also rely on third-party information technology systems in the operation of our business.
Our success depends upon our ability to develop new products for new and existing customers, and to introduce these products in a timely and cost-effective manner.

There may be instances where alternative substances will not be available or commercially feasible, or may only be available from a single source, or may be significantly more expensive than their restricted counterparts – resulting in increased manufacturing costs.
We also rely on trade secrets, proprietary technology, non-disclosure and other contractual terms, and technical measures to protect our technology and manufacturing knowledge.

To the extent the Company has an outstanding balance, our ability to repay the principal of, to pay interest on, or to refinance our indebtedness, depends on our future performance, which is subject to economic, financial, competitive, regulatory, and other factors, some of which are beyond our control.
Our ability to refinance any indebtedness will depend on the capital markets

Any future determination to pay dividends will be made at the discretion of our board of directors, subject to applicable laws, and will depend upon our results of operations, financial condition, contractual restrictions, capital requirements, and other factors.
The timing of the repurchases and the actual amount purchased depend on a variety of factors including general market and economic conditions and other corporate considerations.
